clues: This city stands in the southwest of its state, where a tree lined river cuts through dry high desert. Green banks stand out in the brown, dry land.
Days here can bake past 100 in the dry summer heat. Then the nights drop fast, often more than 30 degrees cooler by dawn.
This town won the territory capital job in a court fight in 1866. A top court kept the seat here by a single vote.
French trappers came on a green, tree lined river in dry country and cried out for the woods. This city's name grew from their French word for wooded land.
The governor of Idaho has his office in this city. State lawmakers meet here each year to run the state.
